people.label: Stephen A. Feinberg
people.narrative: Steve Feinberg is listed on the Department's own site as Deputy Secretary of Defense alongside Secretary Pete Hegseth, and that single organisational fact makes him the most structurally important living official on this board. He is the one official who could answer the central question of this board - whether any waived unacknowledged special access program relates to UAP - from personal knowledge and without consulting anyone.

entities.label: United States Department of Defense (secondary designation: Department of War)
entities.sub: Executive department; owner of the SAP enterprise and of every alleged recovery compartment
entities.desc: The Department of Defense is the institution inside which every alleged element of a legacy recovery and reverse-engineering effort must, by law, sit: the Special Access Program enterprise, the service laboratories, the combat support agencies, and the contracting vehicles that move money to industry. It is also the institution that has produced the entire official denial record. As of 2026 the Department describes itself on its own site as having a budget of $841.4 billion, roughly 3.4 million personnel, and 4,800 sites in over 160 countries, with Pete Hegseth as Secretary and Steve Feinberg as Deputy Secretary. On 5 September 2025 President Trump signed Executive Order 14347, 'Restoring the United States Department of War', authorising 'Department of War' and 'Secretary of War' as secondary designations for use in official correspondence and non-statutory documents while expressly providing that 'Statutory references to the Department of Defense ... shall remain controlling until changed subsequently by the law'; the order directed the Secretary to recommend within 60 days the legislative actions needed to make the rename permanent. The Department's UAP posture runs through three successive offices - the Unidentified Aerial Phenomena Task Force, AOIMSG, and since July 2022 the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office - and through a press-guidance function that has issued the operative denials of Luis Elizondo's AATIP role and of David Grusch's retrieval allegations. The single most important structural fact about DoD for this board is that the Department's own SAP reporting statute, 10 U.S.C. 119, permits the Secretary to waive the reporting of any special access program to the defense committees and instead notify only the chairman and ranking member of each committee - a lawful mechanism by which a program can be run with four members of Congress notified and no one else, which is precisely the mechanism Grusch alleges was abused.

entities.label: DoD Special Access Program Central Office (DoD SAPCO)
entities.sub: Central management office for all DoD special access programs; reports to the Deputy Secretary of Defense
entities.desc: DoD SAPCO is the exact mechanism at issue on this board. Under DoD Directive 5205.07, reissued 12 September 2024 (cancelling the 1 July 2010 version and incorporating the Deputy Secretary of Defense 'SAP Enterprise Reform' memorandum of 11 July 2023), the Special Access Program Central Office operates 'under the authority, direction, and control of the Deputy Secretary of Defense', with a Director who must be a general officer, flag officer, or member of the Senior Executive Service and who reports directly to DEPSECDEF. The Director is the proponent for SAP policy, executive secretary of the Department's SAP governance committees - the Special Access Program Oversight Committee and the Senior Review Group - the primary interagency point of contact for SAP matters, and the office that 'coordinates congressional engagement' on SAPs. Every Office of the Secretary of Defense component, military department and defense agency runs its own subordinate OA SAPCO. Directive 5205.07 also imposes the rule that matters most to this record: personnel must 'notify the Director, DoD SAPCO and OA SAPCO directors' before briefing Congress or congressional staff with SAP material, and no contractor may provide SAP material to Congress without specific approval. That is a legally mandated chokepoint sitting between a program manager and an oversight committee. If a legacy recovery and exploitation effort is carried in the SAP architecture, DoD SAPCO holds the list, the accreditation records, the personnel access rosters and the classification guides for it, and DoD SAPCO is the office that would have to be bypassed for a whistleblower to reach a member of Congress lawfully. AARO's March 2024 historical report states that AARO 'established a partnership with the Special Access Program Control Offices for the DoD, IC, and DHS to review programs identified in interviews by name or description' and that 'AARO investigators have been granted full access to all pertinent sensitive USG programs' - a claim of completeness that rests entirely on the SAPCO enterprise having handed over a complete list. No independent verification of that list has been produced to Congress or the public.

entities.desc: ODNI was created by the Intelligence Reform and Terrorism Prevention Act of 2004 (Public Law 108-458) and stood up on 22 April 2005, placing a Director of National Intelligence above the Intelligence Community elements that had previously answered to the Director of Central Intelligence. For the UAP record ODNI is the co-author of the modern disclosure regime: the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence's report accompanying the Intelligence Authorization Act for FY2021 directed the DNI, in consultation with the Secretary of Defense, to deliver a report on unidentified aerial phenomena, and on 25 June 2021 ODNI published 'Preliminary Assessment: Unidentified Aerial Phenomena'. That nine-page document analysed 144 reports from USG sources, of which 80 involved multiple sensors, and sorted them into five explanatory categories - airborne clutter, natural atmospheric phenomena, USG or U.S. industry developmental programs, foreign adversary systems, and a catch-all 'other'. Its contributor list is itself an intelligence product: USD(I&S), DIA, FBI, NRO, NGA, NSA, the Air Force, the Army, the Navy and ONI, DARPA, FAA, NOAA, ODNI's National Intelligence Manager for Emerging and Disruptive Technology, the National Counterintelligence and Security Center and the National Intelligence Council. ODNI thereafter became a statutory annual reporter on UAP under successive intelligence authorisation acts and NDAAs, and it is one of the four agencies whose records NARA identified in its 24 April 2025 release into the statutory UAP Collection. ODNI is also the parent of the Intelligence Community Inspector General, whose finding that David Grusch's complaint was 'credible and urgent' is the single most consequential procedural act in the modern record.

entities.desc: The NRO is the proof-of-concept for the central claim of this board: that the United States can build, fund and operate a multi-billion-dollar agency for three decades while denying that it exists. Established in 1961 as a joint DoD-CIA activity under a classified DoD directive, the very fact of the NRO's existence was a classified fact until the Deputy Secretary of Defense authorised its disclosure in September 1992; before that, the agency's name could not lawfully be spoken in an unclassified setting, its budget was hidden inside the National Reconnaissance Program, and its headquarters construction at Westfields, Virginia became a congressional scandal in 1994 precisely because the appropriators had not understood what they were funding. Adkins, and it describes its workforce as 31 percent NRO cadre, 34 percent government personnel detailed from other agencies and 35 percent military. For this board the NRO matters three times over. Second, as a collector: ODNI's 2021 Preliminary Assessment lists the NRO among the contributing elements, meaning NRO overhead systems have produced UAP-relevant data. Third, as the employer of the principal witness: David Grusch appeared before the House Oversight Committee on 26 July 2023 under the title 'Former National Reconnaissance Officer Representative, Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Task Force, Department of Defense' - Grusch's access to the UAP Task Force was as the NRO's representative to it, which places the NRO inside the chain of custody of the modern allegation rather than outside it.

entities.label: National Aeronautics and Space Administration
entities.sub: Civil space agency; host of the 2023 UAP Independent Study Team
entities.desc: NASA was created by the National Aeronautics and Space Act of 1958 as an explicitly civilian agency, and for six decades its institutional answer on UFOs was that the subject belonged to the Air Force. That changed on 9 June 2022, when NASA announced an independent study of unidentified anomalous phenomena, and on 14 September 2023, when it published the 'Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Independent Study Team Report'. The 16-member panel was chaired by Dr David Spergel of the Simons Foundation and included Dr Anamaria Berea, Dr Federica Bianco, Dr David Grinspoon and the retired NASA astronaut Captain Scott Kelly. The report's findings are notable less for what they concluded about UAP than for what they conceded about the data problem: that 'much of the data collected by military sensors or intelligence satellites are classified', that structured data curation 'plays a pivotal role' and is largely absent, and that NASA's Earth-observing fleet and the U.S. commercial remote-sensing industry have 'the collective potential to directly resolve UAP events'. In the foreword, Associate Administrator for the Science Mission Directorate Dr Nicola Fox announced that 'NASA is appointing a Director of UAP Research to centralize communications'. NASA's leverage on this board is that it is the one agency with world-class sensing capability, a statutory public mission and no SAP equity in the alleged recovery enterprise - which makes it the most plausible venue for an unclassified evidentiary standard, and the agency most conspicuously kept at arm's length from the classified holdings.

entities.desc: The Air Force is the origin point of the entire American UFO record and of the entire American denial record. Established as an independent service on 18 September 1947 - eleven weeks after the Roswell press release issued by the 509th Bomb Group at Roswell Army Air Field - it inherited Project SIGN (1948), Project GRUDGE (1949) and Project BLUE BOOK (1952-1969) at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio, the same installation that every retrieval account since 1947 identifies as the destination of recovered material. The National Archives records that from 1947 to 1969 'a total of 12,618 sightings were reported to Project BLUE BOOK. Of these 701 remain Unidentified', and that 'On December 17, 1969, the Secretary of the Air Force announced the termination of Project BLUE BOOK', a decision resting on the University of Colorado's 'Scientific Study of Unidentified Flying Objects' and a National Academy of Sciences review of it; the collection now sits at NARA as 94 rolls of 35mm microfilm, T-1206. The Air Force also produced the two modern Roswell rebuttals - 'The Roswell Report: Fact Versus Fiction in the New Mexico Desert' (1994) and 'The Roswell Report: Case Closed' (1997) - which attributed the debris to Project MOGUL and the bodies to anthropomorphic test dummies dropped in the 1950s, an explanation that requires the witnesses to have misdated events by up to a decade. Wright-Patterson remains the home of the Air Force Research Laboratory and of the Foreign Technology Division lineage that became the National Air and Space Intelligence Center, and the Air Force retains the largest single share of the Department's special access program portfolio.

entities.label: Central Intelligence Agency
entities.sub: Independent civilian foreign intelligence service; convener of the Robertson Panel
entities.desc: The CIA was created by the National Security Act of 1947 - signed on 26 July 1947, seventeen days after the Roswell debris story was killed by the Fort Worth weather-balloon photographs - and it is the agency whose documented conduct most nearly matches the pattern this board is built to test. The Agency's own historian, Gerald K. Haines, published 'CIA's Role in the Study of UFOs, 1947-1990' in Studies in Intelligence in 1997; the article is an eighteen-page institutional admission that the Agency ran a UFO effort out of the Office of Scientific Intelligence, convened the Robertson Panel in January 1953 under H. P. Robertson, and adopted a policy of public debunking coupled with the surveillance of civilian UFO organisations. The Robertson Panel's declassified recommendations - that the phenomenon be stripped of its 'aura of mystery' through a programme of 'education' and 'debunking', and that groups such as the Aerial Phenomena Research Organization be monitored 'because of their potentially great influence on mass thinking' - are the founding charter of American UFO information management. Haines additionally records the Agency's later position that U-2 and OXCART overflights accounted for a large share of the UFO reports of the late 1950s and 1960s, a claim that simultaneously excuses the deception and concedes that the Agency knowingly allowed false explanations to stand. The CIA maintains a public FOIA collection, 'UFOs: Fact or Fiction?', which it characterises as containing 'CIA information on this subject from the 1940s through the early 1990s', consisting mostly of 'cables reporting unsubstantiated UFO sightings in the foreign press and intra-Agency memos about how the Agency handled public inquiries'. That framing is itself a claim: it asserts that the Agency's UFO holdings are administrative rather than substantive, and it is the assertion that every subsequent FOIA fight has contested.

entities.label: National Security Agency
entities.sub: Signals intelligence and cybersecurity agency; established 4 November 1952 by classified presidential memorandum
entities.desc: NSA was established on 4 November 1952 by a classified memorandum from President Truman, and like the NRO it spent its early decades as an agency whose name the government preferred not to confirm. Its place in the UAP record is defined by a single piece of litigation that is still the most instructive FOIA case in the field. In Citizens Against UFO Secrecy v. National Security Agency, Civil Action No. 80-1562 in the District Court for the District of Columbia, CAUS sought NSA's UFO holdings; NSA responded by locating a body of responsive material and withholding it in its entirety, supporting the withholding with a classified in camera affidavit executed by Eugene F. Yeates, Chief of NSA's Office of Policy. The public version of the Yeates affidavit was released only in heavily redacted form - the district court reviewed the full text ex parte, the D.C. Circuit affirmed in 1981, and the Supreme Court denied certiorari in 1982. The operative fact is not that NSA won; it is what NSA's own filings conceded in order to win: that the Agency held UFO-related documents, that they were classified, and that the number and nature of them could not be disclosed even to a federal judge in open session. NSA has since released a set of these documents in redacted form, and it appears among the contributing elements listed in ODNI's June 2021 Preliminary Assessment on UAP - confirming that NSA signals collection continues to produce UAP-relevant reporting four decades after it told a court it could not describe what it held.

entities.label: Congressional oversight of special access programs
entities.sub: The statutory oversight mechanism, and the hole in it
entities.desc: Congressional oversight of the Department's most sensitive activities is not a general power; it is a specific statutory scheme with a specific, legally sanctioned exception, and the exception is the whole story. Under 10 U.S.C. 119 the Secretary of Defense must report annually by 1 March to the four defense committees on every special access program, giving for each a brief description, major milestones, actual historical costs and estimated costs through the succeeding four fiscal years, and must notify the committees by 1 February of any newly designated SAP, and must notify them thirty days before initiating a new SAP. But subsection (e) permits the Secretary to waive that reporting where he determines disclosure would harm national security; in that case 'the Secretary shall provide the information described in that subsection with respect to the special access program concerned, and the justification for the waiver, jointly to the chairman and ranking minority member of each of the defense committees.' Eight members of Congress, and no one else. Layered on top of that is DoD Directive 5205.07, which requires any person briefing Congress with SAP material to notify the Director, DoD SAPCO first, and bars contractors from providing SAP material to Congress at all without approval. Layered on top of that is the practical gate described by Chairwoman Luna in September 2025, under which a non-committee member must be approved by the chairman and ranking member of both HASC and HAC-D to see specific material. The result is a structure in which the number of people who can lawfully learn of a waived unacknowledged program is small, fixed, and selected by the department being overseen - and in which a member who suspects a program exists cannot ask for it by name because, as Representative Mace put it, 'if you do not know it, you cannot get the information.' This is the mechanism David Grusch alleges was used, and it is a mechanism that does not require anyone to break the law.

The classification system that governs almost all UAP material is a creature of executive order - currently Executive Order 13526 - which means the President can unilaterally declassify it, and the fact that no President did so for seventy-eight years is a datum about the presidency, not about the material. Successive administrations have touched the file: the Truman administration through the 1947-1952 Air Force projects, the Eisenhower administration through the Robertson Panel, the Carter administration through a 1977 White House inquiry, and the Clinton administration through John Podesta's push for declassification. Executive Order 14347 of 5 September 2025 - the Department of War renaming order - is a reminder of the same power in a different register: the President can rename the department that holds the files by signature, but he cannot by signature reach Restricted Data held under the Atomic Energy Act.

entities.sub: Statutory records collection under sections 1841-1843 of Public Law 118-31
entities.desc: The UAP Records Collection is what survived the Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Disclosure Act. Sections 1841 to 1843 of the FY2024 National Defense Authorization Act, Public Law 118-31, directed the creation at the National Archives of a collection of United States Government records relating to unidentified anomalous phenomena, modelled on the JFK Assassination Records Collection - but stripped in conference of the independent review board with subpoena power and of the eminent domain provision that would have compelled private holders of recovered material to surrender it. NARA established the collection as Record Group 615 and announced on 24 April 2025 that it had released records transferred from four agencies - the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, the Office of the Secretary of Defense, the Federal Aviation Administration and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission - and that it 'will continue to add UAP records to the Collection and make them available online through the National Archives Catalog on an ongoing, rolling basis'. The composition of that first transfer is itself evidence: two of the four contributing agencies are civilian regulators. entities.desc: NNSA is 'a semi-autonomous agency within the U.S. Department of Energy responsible for enhancing national security through the military application of nuclear science', established by Congress in 2000 in the wake of the Wen Ho Lee security failures at Los Alamos. It operates the weapons complex through management and operating contracts: Los Alamos National Laboratory, Sandia National Laboratories, Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, the Nevada National Security Site, the Pantex Plant, the Y-12 National Security Complex, the Kansas City National Security Campus and the Savannah River Site. Every one of those facilities is contractor-operated on government-owned land, carries an armed protective force, operates under DOE's own clearance regime rather than the DoD's, and holds material under Restricted Data authority. entities.label: Waived unacknowledged special access program (waived USAP)
entities.sub: The specific legal category at the centre of every allegation on this board
entities.desc: A waived unacknowledged special access program is the most protected category of activity the United States government operates. Special access programs are activities requiring protection beyond that ordinarily required for information at the same classification level, imposing need-to-know controls, access rosters and separate security architecture; DoD Directive 5205.07 governs them. An unacknowledged SAP is one whose existence is not acknowledged - the response to an inquiry is neither confirmation nor denial. A waived SAP is one for which the Secretary of Defense has exercised the waiver at 10 U.S.C. 119(e), under which the annual report and the justification for the waiver go 'jointly to the chairman and ranking minority member of each of the defense committees' instead of to the committees as a whole. Combine the two and the result is an activity whose existence is denied to the public, denied to most of Congress, and known in the legislative branch to eight people. Every serious allegation on this board reduces to a claim about this category: David Grusch's testimony that a multi-decade materials recovery and exploitation effort exists and is unreported; the 2009 Reid request that AAWSAP be granted restricted SAP status, which USD(I) James Clapper opposed; the 2011 DHS attempt to stand up KONA BLUE as a prospective SAP; and the FY2024 NDAA section 1687 limitation on the use of funds for UAP-related programs not reported to the congressional defense committees, which is Congress legislating directly against the possibility that this category has been abused.

dod-sapco.desc: The mechanism, stated plainly. Three documents define the space in which a concealed program could lawfully live. (1) 10 U.S.C. 119: annual SAP report to the four defense committees by 1 March; new-SAP notification by 1 February; 30 days notice before initiation - unless the Secretary waives it, in which case the information and the waiver justification go 'jointly to the chairman and ranking minority member of each of the defense committees'. Eight members. (2) DoD Directive 5205.07, reissued 12 September 2024, cancelling the 1 July 2010 version and incorporating the DEPSECDEF SAP Enterprise Reform memorandum of 11 July 2023: DoD SAPCO sits under the authority, direction and control of the Deputy Secretary of Defense; its Director is a GO/FO/SES reporting directly to DEPSECDEF, is executive secretary of the SAP governance committees, and 'coordinates congressional engagement'; and any person briefing Congress or congressional staff with SAP material must notify the Director, DoD SAPCO first, while contractors may not provide such material to Congress without specific approval. (3) The read-in practice described on the record by Chairwoman Anna Paulina Luna on 9 September 2025: a non-committee member must be approved by the chairman and ranking member of both HASC and HAC-D. Composed, these produce a structure in which the office administering a program is notified before the overseer is briefed, the contractor holding it is barred from talking to Congress, and the members entitled to know can be counted on two hands. Nothing in that sequence requires anyone to break the law.

waived-usap.desc: Terms of art, precisely. A special access program imposes protection beyond that required for information at the same classification level - access rosters, separate billets, dedicated security architecture. An ACKNOWLEDGED SAP appears in the budget by name with a classified purpose. An UNACKNOWLEDGED SAP is one whose existence is not confirmed; the correct response to an inquiry is neither confirmation nor denial. A WAIVED unacknowledged SAP adds the 10 U.S.C. 119(e) waiver, which removes the program from the report to the defense committees and substitutes notification to the chairman and ranking member of each. Every substantive allegation on this board resolves into one of exactly two propositions: that a materials acquisition and exploitation activity exists as a waived USAP known to eight members of Congress, or that it exists outside the SAP system entirely and is therefore unlawful. The first is testable by demanding the waived-SAP list. The second is testable by an ISOO NISP audit of cleared facilities. Neither test has been run.

doe.desc: Why DOE is the hardest problem on the board. Restricted Data and Formerly Restricted Data are created by the Atomic Energy Act of 1954 and are classified by operation of statute - 'born classified' - rather than by an original classification authority acting under an executive order. The practical consequences are three. First, a presidential declassification directive that operates on Executive Order 13526 information does not reach RD/FRD; the February 2026 UAP directive is such a directive. Second, RD/FRD is administered jointly by DOE and DoD under a separate procedure requiring DOE concurrence, so DoD cannot unilaterally release it either.
